items.readme:
# ESP32 iPhone Agent **Let an AI model use a real iPhone — with a $7 ESP32. No Mac, no developer account, no jailbreak.** English · [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) Demo video and updates: [X @iamhenryyuan](https://x.com/iamhenryyuan) · [YouTube demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ly4im-P4jYg) [![CI](https://github.com/onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](LICENSE) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue) ![Board](https://img.shields.io/badge/board-ESP32--S3-red)

**Example 1 — draw on a canvas.** *"Open Whiteboard and draw a smiley face"*: the agent searches for the app, opens it and draws the face with continuous strokes. Every step's screenshot, with its tap or stroke drawn on top, stays on the step wall.

**Example 2 — set an alarm.** *"Set an alarm for 7:00 AM that repeats every day, then save it"*: the agent opens Clock, types 0700 into the time wheel, ticks the days under Repeat several taps at a time, and saves. Left: the real iPhone with the ESP32 plugged in; right: the web UI. The agent sees the phone through AirPlay screen mirroring and touches it through a tiny ESP32-S3 board that plugs into the phone's USB port as a mouse and keyboard. Any OpenAI-compatible vision model can be the brain — a cloud API, or a model you run yourself. ## Why Most iPhone automation drives the phone through XCTest / WebDriverAgent. That needs a Mac, Xcode, a signed helper app and an Apple developer account (a free account's signature expires every 7 days). This project uses the same paths a person uses — the screen and a pointer — so the phone needs nothing installed. | | ESP32 iPhone Agent | XCTest / WebDriverAgent tools | |----------------------------------|---------------------------|-------------------------------| | Apple developer account | **Not needed** | Needed (to sign the runner) | | Xcode | **Not needed** | Needed | | Computer | Mac **or Linux** | Mac | | App installed on the phone | **None** | Test runner app | | Jailbreak | Not needed | Not needed | | Extra hardware | ESP32-S3 board (~$7) | USB cable | | Works in any app, incl. games | Yes (it only sees pixels) | Mostly (depends on the accessibility tree) | ## How it works - **Eyes — AirPlay mirroring.** The phone mirrors its screen to [UxPlay](https://github.com/FDH2/UxPlay) running on your computer; a GStreamer pipeline turns the stream into JPEG frames for the agent and the web page. - **Hands — a USB HID bridge.** An ESP32-S3 plugged into the phone shows up as a standard USB mouse and keyboard. With iOS AssistiveTouch on, the mouse moves an on-screen pointer, so a click is a tap and a drag is a swipe. The board connects to the computer over Wi-Fi and executes simple line commands (`move`, `click`, `type`, …); all logic stays on the computer. - **Brain — a planner and an actor.** A planner model writes a short plan from the goal and the current screen. An actor model then looks at each new screenshot and picks the next action: tap, swipe, draw a path, type, press a key, go home, or finish. Both roles can be the same model. - **Closing the loop.** The pointer is relative, so the server tracks where it is. Before each tap it wiggles the pointer, finds it on the mirrored screen and corrects any miss, refining the calibration as it goes. After each action it checks whether the screen actually changed and tells the model, so a missed tap is noticed and retried instead of built upon. Repeated actions trigger a re-plan; a dropped link or a bad reply is recovered from. ## Hardware | Part | Notes | |---|---| | **ESP32-S3 board** | Tested with a [Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32S3](https://wiki.seeedstudio.com/xiao_esp32s3_getting_started/), plain version without pre-soldered headers (not the Sense camera version, not the Plus). About $7 from Seeed, or about ¥40-50 on Taobao in China (search "XIAO ESP32S3"). Any ESP32-S3 board whose USB-C port is wired to the S3's native USB works. | | **iPhone** | USB-C models plug in directly. Lightning models need a Lightning to USB Camera Adapter. The phone powers the board. | | **Computer** | macOS or Linux, on the same network as the phone; runs UxPlay and the server. | | **Vision model** | Any OpenAI-compatible chat API that accepts images. Running a model locally is optional. |

Use a USB-C hub with power pass-through if the phone should keep charging while the board is plugged in. ## Quick start > **Set up with an AI coding agent.** Paste this into Claude Code, Codex or a similar agent on the computer the > board will connect to: > > ```text > Clone https://github.com/onehumanbeing/esp32-iphone-agent and follow its README to set it up on this machine: > flash the ESP32-S3 plugged in over USB, install UxPlay and the server, write server/.env for my model API, start > the server and give me the web UI address. Ask me for the Wi-Fi name/password and the model API key. > ``` ### 1. Flash the board Install [arduino-cli](https://arduino.github.io/arduino-cli/) and the ESP32 core (3.x), then: ```bash cp hardware/hid_bridge/secrets.example.h hardware/hid_bridge/secrets.h # edit secrets.h: 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi name/password and the IP address of the computer running the server hardware/flash.sh # optional arguments: [serial port] [--debug] ``` ### 2. Install and start the server ```bash # UxPlay — macOS: brew install uxplay # UxPlay — Debian / Ubuntu: sudo apt install uxplay gstreamer1.0-plugins-good gstreamer1.0-plugins-bad gstreamer1.0-libav cd server python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -e . cp .env.example .env # set LLM_BASE_URL / LLM_MODEL / LLM_API_KEY set -a && . ./.env && set +a && .venv/bin/python -m hidagent ``` Open `http://:8890` in a browser. ### 3. Set up the phone (once) 1. **Settings → Accessibility → Touch → AssistiveTouch**: turn it on. 2. Plug the board into the phone. A round pointer appears; the web page shows *controller connected*. 3. **Control Center → Screen Mirroring → iPhone Agent**. The live screen appears in the web page. 4. In the web page, open **Manual controls → Calibrate**. The server moves the pointer, finds it on the live screen and calibrates itself in a few seconds; if it cannot see the pointer, it asks you to click exactly on it. ### 4. Give it a task Type a goal (for example *"Open Settings and go to Wi-Fi"*) and press **Start**, or click one of the examples. ## Web UI - **Live phone** — click to tap, drag to swipe, scroll to scroll; manual Home, Back, typing and keys. - **Live log** — every plan, thought and action as it happens, with timings. - **Step wall** — the screenshot the model decided on for every step, with its tap or swipe drawn on top, plus the model's reasoning and how long thinking and acting took. Click a card to zoom in. - **Taps** are marked with a red ring and a spreading ripple, swipes and strokes with a yellow path; the **Motion** switch turns the animation off. Taps the model marked `precise` (pointer checked before tapping) are labelled in the log. - **Emergency stop** (or Esc) stops the agent and releases the pointer. **Clear history** empties the log. - English and Simplified Chinese interface. ## Configuration Set in `server/.env` (see [`.env.example`](server/.env.example)): | Variable | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `LLM_BASE_URL` | `http://localhost:8000/v1` | OpenAI-compatible endpoint | | `LLM_MODEL` / `LLM_API_KEY` | — | Model name and API key | | `LLM_EXTRA_BODY` | `{}` | JSON merged into every request (e.g. to turn off a model's thinking mode) | | `LLM_TOKEN_PARAM` | `auto` | Token-limit field: `max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens` (newer OpenAI models), or `auto` to detect | | `ACTOR_*` / `PLANNER_*` | — | Per-role overrides of any `LLM_*` variable | | `AIRPLAY_NAME` | `iPhone Agent` | Receiver name in the phone's Screen Mirroring list | | `PORT` / `DEVICE_PORT` | `8890` / `7300` | Web UI port / port the board connects to | | `HIDAGENT_DATA` | `~/.hidagent` | Calibration and debug traces | | `HIDAGENT_DEBUG` | `0` | Debug mode, see below | ### Local model (optional) A cloud API is enough. If you want everything on your own hardware, this is the setup the project was developed and timed with: - Model: [nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) - Serving: [Qwen3.8-Flash-Dual-DGX-Sparks-TensorFold](https://github.com/MiaAI-Lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Dual-DGX-Sparks-TensorFold) — two NVIDIA DGX Sparks with tensor parallelism (TP=2), OpenAI-compatible API - Speed: about 1.3 s per action and 2 s per plan, with thinking mode off: ```bash LLM_BASE_URL=http://:8888/v1 LLM_MODEL=Qwen3.8-Flash-Next LLM_EXTRA_BODY='{"chat_template_kwargs": {"enable_thinking": false}}' ``` Any other OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, …) with a vision model works the same way. ## Debug mode Set `HIDAGENT_DEBUG=1` to log every board command with its latency and to save one folder per agent run: ``` ~/.hidagent/traces/20261012-005207/ ├── steps.jsonl # every model call (prompt, raw reply, latency) and every action ├── 002.jpg # the screenshot each model call saw └── ... ``` `hardware/flash.sh --debug` builds firmware that echoes each command and its duration over USB serial. ## Board protocol The board holds no logic. On connecting it sends `hello `; then the server sends one command per line over TCP and the board answers `ok` or `err `. | Command | Effect | |---|---| | `ping` | Health check | | `home` | Push the pointer into the top-left corner (a known position) | | `move ` | Relative pointer move, at a constant pace so iOS pointer acceleration stays predictable | | `press` / `release` / `click` | Left button down / up / both | | `scroll ` | Scroll wheel | | `type ` | Type ASCII text | | `key ` | Press keys, e.g. `enter`, `cmd+h`, `cmd+space` | If the Wi-Fi link drops, the board releases all buttons and reconnects on its own. While the phone is locked, its USB port sleeps: the board then tries to wake it and otherwise answers `err phone usb asleep` instead of waiting. A watchdog restarts the board if it ever stops responding. ## Project layout ``` hardware/ ESP32-S3 firmware (Arduino) and flash script server/ agent, web UI, screen capture and board link (Python, FastAPI) serve/: optional minimal server to host a Hugging Face vision model yourself ``` ## Roadmap - [ ] Test a fully local setup with DiffusionGemma (`server/serve/` has an experimental OpenAI-compatible server) - [ ] Landscape apps (screen coordinates and calibration assume portrait) - [ ] Non-ASCII text input (e.g. Chinese through the iOS pinyin keyboard) - [ ] More example tasks across popular apps ### Exploring: drop the computer Right now the board is just the hands. The brain and the eyes run on a separate computer. The next idea is to drop the computer. Swap the ESP32 for a small board that can run Linux, and run the whole loop on it: see the screen, decide, tap. The phone would only need that one board, which you could carry in your pocket. The board could talk to the phone over USB or Bluetooth, and call a local or cloud model. These are directions, not promises. If you're interested, or you've tried something similar, open an issue. ## Limitations - iOS does not mirror some screens (passcode entry, Apple Pay, DRM video); the agent cannot see them. - Mirroring stops when the phone locks; keep auto-lock off while the agent works. - Keyboard input is ASCII only. - Re-calibrate after changing AssistiveTouch tracking speed. - Landscape apps are not supported yet: drawings and taps there land in the wrong place. - On Linux machines with several network interfaces, limit Avahi (mDNS) to the interface on the phone's network if the phone does not list the receiver. ## Responsible use Only automate devices and accounts you own or are allowed to use, and respect the terms of the apps involved. The agent acts with your hands: watch it, and keep the emergency stop within reach. ## Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome. Run the checks before sending a change: ```bash cd server && pip install -e ".[dev]" && ruff check . && pytest ``` ## Related projects Other ways people drive an iPhone with code or AI, and how this project differs. Corrections welcome. | Project | Approach | Needs on the phone / host | Difference from this project | |---|---|---|---| | [VersaiOS](https://github.com/zhaodashuaibi/VersaiOS) | UxPlay mirroring + ESP32-S3 Bluetooth mouse + vision model | ESP32 tethered to a computer over USB serial; desktop GUI, mainly Windows | Closest in spirit. One tap per instruction, no planning step or before/after screen check | | [ja1chen/actell](https://github.com/ja1chen/actell) | Agent app on the iPhone, screenshots and taps via Apple's CoreDevice debug channel | Developer Mode, pairing + Developer Disk Image, Xcode self-signing | This project needs no Developer Mode, no app on the phone and no signing | | [AidenAI-IO/aiden-firmware](https://github.com/AidenAI-IO/aiden-firmware) | Dedicated board: HDMI capture + USB keyboard/mouse + multimodal model | HDMI capture chip and dock; mainly Android | Uses AirPlay instead of HDMI capture, so no capture hardware | | [yoyicue/glassbox](https://github.com/yoyicue/glassbox) | PicoKVM HDMI capture + USB HID, observe/decide/act/verify loop | macOS controller and PicoKVM | Runs on Linux with a single ESP32 | | [boboabw/phone-agent](https://github.com/boboabw/phone-agent) | ESP32-S3 Bluetooth HID + AssistiveTouch, agent runs as an iPhone app | Mac + Xcode to build and sign the app | Nothing to install on the phone | | [dovydaskel/Iphone-control-for-social-media](https://github.com/dovydaskel/Iphone-control-for-social-media) | ESP32 Bluetooth mouse with OpenCV pointer correction, scripted posting | Mac | Similar closed-loop pointer idea; this project adds a vision-model planner/executor | | [VKCOM/devicehub](https://github.com/VKCOM/devicehub) | ESP32 Bluetooth mouse for iOS device farms | Farm infrastructure | Device-farm tooling, no AI agent | | [NolanCotter/AirBridge](https://github.com/NolanCotter/AirBridge) / [gbulog/pcairplay](https://github.com/gbulog/pcairplay) | UxPlay on Linux + the PC's own Bluetooth as keyboard/mouse | Linux PC with Bluetooth | Manual remote control, no AI | Other routes: WebDriverAgent/XCUITest-based tools such as [mobile-mcp](https://github.com/mobile-next/mobile-mcp) and [Midscene](https://github.com/web-infra-dev/midscene) need a Mac and code signing; tools built on macOS iPhone Mirroring need a Mac. ## Acknowledgements [UxPlay](https://github.com/FDH2/UxPlay) (AirPlay receiver) · [Arduino ESP32 core](https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32) and [TinyUSB](https://github.com/hathach/tinyusb) (USB HID) · [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

items.name: fsearch
items.description: Whole-disk file search for macOS: fuzzy names, typo tolerance, indexed content grep. ~1 ms over 8M files.
items.readme:
# FSearch

Whole-disk file search for macOS. Finds any file by name in about a
millisecond, forgives typos, and searches inside files with an index. Use it
as a CLI (with a small daemon) or as a Rust crate.

```
cargo build --release && ./target/release/fsearch install   # -> ~/.local/bin/fsearch
fsearch fsearch main              # find files by name
fsearch 'ext:rs grep:apply_dir'   # search inside files
```

## Speed

M4 Max, 7.7M files and folders on disk.

| | |
|---|---|
| find a file by name, whole disk | p50 1.3 ms |
| search inside files | p50 9 ms |
| a new, renamed or deleted file shows up | ~0.1 s |
| first crawl of the disk | ~20 s, once |
| daemon memory | 30-135 MB |

## vs fff

Chromium (509k files), same Mac, same queries. Video:
[`demo/fsearch-vs-fff.mp4`](demo/fsearch-vs-fff.mp4), method:
[`demo/vs_fff.py`](demo/vs_fff.py).

| | fsearch | [fff](https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff) |
|---|---|---|
| find a file by name | 1.1 ms | 13.8 ms |
| search inside files | 5.6 ms | 53 ms |
| typo still finds the file first | 98% | 88% |
| ready after launch | 50 ms | 2.5 s |
| memory | 50 MB (whole disk) | 358 MB (that folder) |

On the smaller Linux kernel (96k files), name search is a tie and fsearch
wins the rest. fff searches the contents of about 9% more files, because
fsearch skips some file types and `build/` and `vendor/` folders.

## Queries

```
fsearch 'readme in:~/Developer'          # inside a folder
fsearch 'type:image size:>5mb mtime:<7d'
fsearch 'ext:rs regex:fn\s+\w+_dir'      # regex inside files
fsearch 'sym:apply_dir'                  # where it's defined
```

Words are fuzzy, and 5+ letter words forgive one typo (`mian.rs` finds
`main.rs`). Also `'exact`, `^prefix`, `suffix$` and `!exclude`. Filters:
`ext:` `type:` `kind:` `in:` `size:` `mtime:` `re:` `path:` `grep:` `regex:`
`sym:` `limit:`. Content search is smart-case.

## Full Disk Access

Started from a terminal with Full Disk Access, it indexes everything. As a
login item (`fsearch install --login`), give `~/.local/bin/fsearch` its own
grant in System Settings > Privacy & Security, again after each rebuild.
Without access it skips the protected folders instead of popping a prompt.

## API

JSON lines over `~/Library/Application Support/FSearch/fsearch.sock`, or
`fsearch stdio`:

```json
{"q": "fsearch main", "limit": 20}
{"op": "grep", "pattern": "apply_dir", "in": "~/Developer"}
```

Or link the crate:

```rust
let engine = fsearch::Engine::start(fsearch::Options { dir: fsearch::default_dir(&home), home: home.clone(), skip: None })?;
let hits = engine.search(&fsearch::Query::parse("fsearch main", &home)?)?;
```

An app and the CLI share one index: the first process owns it and the
others follow along.

## How it works

- Crawls the disk once with `getattrlistbulk`, then stays current from
  FSEvents. A restart replays only what changed.
- Names live in one mmap'd file, laid out folder by folder so `in:` is a
  range. Each distinct name is scored once.
- Content search uses a trigram index of your text files. Matches are read
  fresh from disk, so they're never stale.

items.name: d2r-mobile
items.description: Open-source iOS / macOS compatibility layer for Diablo II: Resurrected with the Reign of the Warlock expansion. Runs your own Switch copy natively on iPhone, iPad and Mac — full touch controls, 60 fps, new endgame modes. Bring your own game files. 开源的《暗黑破坏神 II：狱火重生》术士君临 iOS / macOS 兼容层
items.readme:
# D2R Mobile **An open-source iOS compatibility layer for Diablo II: Resurrected with the Reign of the Warlock expansion.** It brings the Nintendo Switch release you bought, expansion included, to iPhone and iPad in full: the original game code runs natively, every control is rebuilt for touch, the frame rate holds at 60 fps, and you are in a game one second after the main menu. This is not a tech demo that "sort of runs". It is a mobile version polished for daily play, from your first character all the way through the endgame. Platforms: iPhone / iPad (iOS 26 and later) · Game version: Switch release with Reign of the Warlock, 3.3.94012 · English / 中文 · License: MIT · **Bring your own game files** 中文: [README.zh-CN.md](README.zh-CN.md)

| 100% | 60 fps | about 1 s | about 3.8 W | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | The original gameplay, because it is the original program | Steady, with no drops once the device warms up | From the main menu into a game | Whole-device power draw at 60 fps | ## What it is, and what it is not **It is:** - The game's own aarch64 program, **executing directly on the device**, with no emulated CPU. iPhone and Switch use the same class of processor; only the handful of instructions that cannot run unchanged under Apple's kernel are rewritten, and every other byte of the program is left exactly as shipped. Every class, every Runeword, Terror Zones, bosses, drop rules and quest flow are identical to the original. - The platform services the game expects — system calls, the file system, the graphics API, audio, input — provided by a small host written for Apple platforms. The graphics API is reimplemented entirely on Apple's Metal with no emulation layer in between, and the shaders are translated offline from the game's originals. - A port built for phones, and taken all the way: a complete touch control scheme, edge-to-edge iPhone and true full-screen iPad display, controller support, a power saver mode, save sync, English and Chinese, and a whole set of endgame modes and quality-of-life features the original never had. **It is not:** - An emulator, cloud gaming, or streaming. - **A source of game content. It contains none and distributes none.** There is no game program, art, text, data table or shader in this repository; all of that is generated on your own machine from your own files (see [docs/GAME_FILES.md](docs/GAME_FILES.md)). What the repository does carry is the interface information we recorded to make the port work — shader interface descriptions, the graphics API function table, addresses inside the program and the like — listed item by item in [docs/DERIVED.md](docs/DERIVED.md). - Online. There is no multiplayer; the game runs fully offline and needs no online account. ## Battle-tested All **44** iPhones and iPads in the closed beta — 35 devices registered for direct install (25 iPhones and 10 iPads), plus 9 TestFlight accounts with one device each — **completed Normal, Nightmare and Hell with multiple characters**, and the experience was excellent. From an iPhone 14 Pro Max with 6 GB of memory to the latest iPad Pro, not one device fell behind. | | Models | |---|---| | iPhone | 14 Pro Max, 15, 15 Pro, 15 Pro Max, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, 16 Pro Max, 17 Pro Max and more | | iPad | iPad Air, iPad mini, iPad Pro 11-inch and 12.9 / 13-inch (including M2 and M4) and more | | Lowest model tested | **iPhone 14 Pro Max (A16, 6 GB): a flawless 60 fps** | iPhone and iPad share a single install package.

## Fast, smooth, and easy on the battery Measured on a real device (iPhone 17 Pro Max): | Item | Reading | |---|---| | In-game frame rate | **60 fps**, steady, with no drops once the device warms up | | App launch | 0.15 s | | To the main menu | about 1 s | | From the main menu into a game | **about 1 s** | | Quick Restart, back in a game | about 1.2 s | | Longest frame when changing acts | about 0.1 s | | Whole-device power, 60 fps | **about 3.8 W** (in camp, 50% brightness): nearly 5 hours of continuous play on a full charge | | Whole-device power, power saver mode at 30 fps | **about 1.85 W**, about half the 60 fps figure, for about twice the battery life | Measurement conditions: power is whole-device power measured on 2026-10-10 on an iPhone 17 Pro Max, standing in the Act I camp at 50% brightness, with 60 fps and power saver mode measured in the same scene; battery life is calculated from the measured power and the battery capacity, not by playing from full to empty. Launch and game-entry times were measured on the same model in 2026-10; frame rate and act-change readings were taken on the same model on 2026-10-12 while moving through areas and changing acts after entering a game. The install package is only a little over 100 MB. The game resources (about 5.6 GB) are placed on the phone separately, and updating the app touches neither your saves nor the resources. Why it is this fast: the program executes natively, and not a single instruction goes through emulation; graphics go straight to Metal; every shader is translated offline and compiled ahead of time, so nothing is compiled when you enter a new scene. Older chips such as the A16 do not support the game's original compressed texture format, so we built a supplementary texture pack for them, and they run at full frame rate too. ## Redesigned for fingers This is not a gamepad pasted onto the screen. Every panel and every action was rebuilt for fingers under one design principle: **keep the original interface language, and use gestures instead of adding buttons to the screen**. Text sizes and tap targets are sized for fingers. You know how to play the moment you pick it up, and it stays comfortable over long sessions.

- **Move**: a virtual stick with precise diagonals; tap an NPC or the ground to path there automatically; doors, portals and cave entrances are tappable across their whole surface. - **Fight**: press a skill button to cast, hold to keep casting, **drag to aim at any angle**; nearby monsters are targeted automatically. Two skill sets. Skills on your secondary weapons cast with one tap — the game swaps weapons, casts, and swaps back — and the button shows the charges remaining. - **Boss health bar**: pinned to the top of the screen, showing the percentage remaining. - **Items**: tap, double-tap, long-press and drag and drop all track your finger. Double-tap gear to equip or unequip it; drag an item anywhere onto the vendor panel to sell it; on a stack, double-tap takes 1 and long-press takes 3; long-press an empty inventory slot to sort everything. - **Text**: typed with the system keyboard. Character names can be in Chinese; leave the name blank for a random one. - **Screen**: on iPhone the 19.5:9 display is filled edge to edge, clear of the notch and rounded corners; on iPad the game fills the entire screen, and the interface centers itself when you open a panel; the 3D picture can be brightened. ### Controller Connect a controller and press any button: the interface switches to the original controller layout, with button prompts at the bottom of every panel. Touch the screen and you are back in the touch interface instantly. Inventory, stash, skill tree, Chronicle and settings are fully controller-navigable, with the same button mapping as on Switch.

## New ways to play, on top of the original Finishing the original game is only the beginning. Without touching the original rules, we added a full set of endgame content that keeps you farming. ### Greater Rift Enter through the red portal in Harrogath after completing Hell. There are 100 levels, and the monsters grow stronger with each one; fill the progress bar and slay the Rift Guardian within 15 minutes to clear a level. Every 2 levels cleared grants +1 Skill Point and +5 Stat Points, and the skill level cap rises from 20 to 40. Every 10 levels has a first-clear reward, and clearing level 10 unlocks six new equipment slots for your mercenary.

### Endgame Boss Rush, Elysium mode, and the Kill Board - **Endgame Boss Rush**: unlocks after completing Hell, with 12 stages; stage 11 is Diablo Clone, and stage 12 is the three Uber bosses. - **Elysium mode** (chosen at character creation): Unique ×5, Set ×3, Runes ×5; the "no drop" chance is cut to a tenth, and bosses always drop as on a first kill. - **Kill Board**: for every boss, the number of kills, the time of the first kill, how many Unique and Set items it has dropped, and your best and average kill times.

### Storage: a collector's paradise - **Chronicle stash**: every identified Unique and Set item has its own fixed slot, shared by all characters, searchable, with deposit and withdraw; the Deposit button sends the Unique and Set items in your inventory and Horadric Cube there in one tap. - **Stash**: widened to 14 columns, with 5 personal pages and 5 shared pages. - **Trove**: the gem, rune and material pages merged into one, with the Horadric Cube's crafting grid in the middle, so finding things and crafting no longer means flipping between pages. Runes, gems and materials you put into the personal or shared pages are filed here automatically. - **Pouch**: an extended inventory. Runes and gems found in the field go into it automatically and take up no inventory space.

### Effortless farming | | | |---|---| | Auto-recast buffs | Buff skills you have learned do not need a slot on the skill bar: when a buff runs out, it is recast the moment you stand still; buffs that come from your secondary weapons (such as Battle Orders from Call to Arms) swap weapons, recast and swap back on their own | | Potions and belt | Auto-drink has two tiers: a healing potion below 50% Life, a rejuvenation potion below 30%; **your mercenary is fed automatically by the same rule**. Potions on the ground are picked up automatically when the belt has room; double-tap an empty belt slot to refill the whole belt | | Loot filter | From Nightmare on, the original loot filter is switched on automatically to hide clutter: light filtering in Nightmare, heavy in Hell | | Auto-pickup | Low runes and gems go straight into the Pouch; the high ones are left for you to pick up yourself | | Valuable drop alerts | High runes and Unique items raise a light beam and land with a different drop sound; the phone vibrates at one of three strengths — light, medium or heavy — according to value | | Runeword helper | Long-press a socketed base to list the Runewords it can make and their stats; once you have the runes, socket them all in one tap | | Minimap guidance | Every map marks its Waypoint and exits; every quest goal is on the map; when a target is off screen, its name is written along the screen edge | | Chores removed | Free identification, free Town Portal with no scrolls needed, spawning right beside the Waypoint, Quick Restart, refreshable vendor stock | | Saves | Saved immediately when you switch apps, swipe the app away or quit; iCloud sync across devices (requires signing with a paid developer account) | Most features can be toggled one by one in game under Options → Custom.

### English and Chinese The whole game switches between English and Chinese under Options → Custom; after a restart, both the interface and the voice acting are in the language you chose. In English, items, skills and monsters use the original Diablo II wording, and everything we added — Greater Rift, Chronicle, the settings page, controller prompts — is in English too.

## How it works ```mermaid flowchart LR G["Your game files
(program + resources)"] --> P["Rewriter
changes only a few instructions"] G --> S["Shader translation
original → Metal"] P --> H["Host
system services"] S --> X["Graphics layer
the graphics API on Metal"] H --> A["iOS app
touch and interface"] X --> A ``` | Part | Where | What it does | |---|---|---| | Program rewriter | `dm/tools/patch_nso.py` | Rewrites only the few instructions that cannot run unchanged under Apple's kernel (thread-pointer registers, system calls, timers) and leaves the rest of the program byte-for-byte as shipped | | Host | `dm/host` | Loads the rewritten program and provides the platform services it calls | | Graphics | `dm/gfx` | Implements the game's graphics API on Metal; shaders are translated offline from the game's originals | | iOS app | `dm/ios` | The app shell, touch controls and interface | | Verification | `dm/verify` | Checks that the rewritten code behaves exactly like the original, plus the regression gates every change goes through | **Why you can trust it:** the stability is not luck. The test and verification tooling is part of the project — unit tests for the host and graphics layers, an equivalence check for every rewritten instruction, scripted walkthrough regression for the touch interface, and on-device smoke tests. Start with `make -C dm/host/tests run`, `make -C dm/gfx/tests run` and `dm/verify/regress.sh` (run them inside the Python environment prepared in step 2 below; `regress.sh` also needs `brew install llvm`). How to contribute is in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ## Getting started Both routes start with **the files of the game you bought**: the Switch release of Diablo II: Resurrected plus the Reign of the Warlock expansion, updated to 3.3.94012. This project is built for the version with that expansion; using it without the expansion is not supported and has not been verified. How to prepare them is in [docs/GAME_FILES.md](docs/GAME_FILES.md). | | With a Mac | Without a Mac | |---|---|---| | Computer | An Apple silicon Mac with Xcode installed | Windows / Linux / a Mac without Xcode | | Method | A full build from source | Download a "shell" with no game content, use the packaging tool to add your own game content, then install it with a sideloading tool | | Status | The main route; everything above comes from it | Works end to end on Windows, from making the package to playing on a device, and the game program produced on the two systems is byte-for-byte identical; the one step nobody has tried yet is signing with a sideloading tool — try it and tell us | | Instructions | The three steps below | [docs/NO_XCODE.md](docs/NO_XCODE.md) | The Apple account used for signing: a paid developer account gives you everything; a free Apple ID works too (no iCloud save sync, and the app has to be re-signed and reinstalled every 7 days). The full list of dependencies is in [docs/DEPENDENCIES.md](docs/DEPENDENCIES.md). ### With a Mac: three steps 1. Put your game files in the workspace (default `~/dm-work`, or set `DM_ROOT`): ``` ~/dm-work/data/switch/3.3.94012/Update/ExeFS/ main, sdk, subsdk0 ~/dm-work/data/switch/3.3.94012/Update/RomFS/ data/… ``` 2. Prepare the workspace. This checks your tools, rewrites the game program, and translates the game's shaders to Metal. The first run takes a while; later runs skip what is already done. ``` ./setup.sh source ~/dm-work/build/cache/dm/venv/bin/activate # run everything after this inside the Python environment setup prepared; if you changed DM_ROOT, use it in place of ~/dm-work ``` 3. Fill in your signing details and build the app: ``` cp dm/ios/local.env.example dm/ios/local.env # set DM_TEAM_ID and DM_BUNDLE_ID; with a free Apple ID also set DM_FREE_ACCOUNT=1 and DM_IOS_UDID, and keep the phone connected while building cd dm/ios && ./run.sh build # targets both iPhone and iPad by default; for iPhone only: DM_DEVICE_FAMILY=1 ./run.sh build ``` The first time you open the app on your phone, it asks for the "game resource folder" — the 18 resource archives from your game files. Where to put them is in the section "The "game resource folder" that goes on the phone" of [docs/GAME_FILES.md](docs/GAME_FILES.md). `./setup.sh check` is a health check: it reports the state of this computer, the tools, the game files and the signing configuration item by item, and for everything missing it says where to get it and which command to run next; it changes nothing. If what you have is a whole game package (`.xci` / `.nsp`), `./setup.sh ` first extracts the game files into place and then carries on (install hactool first). Run `./setup.sh` again after every update to a new commit: it rebuilds the patched binaries and the shader library for the current sources (steps that are already up to date are skipped). It also rewrites three files in the repository that change with your local tool fingerprints (`dm/gfx/tools/dmsh_chain.lock`, `dm/gfx/nvn/dmsh_chain.h`, `dm/gfx/nvn/c1_full.tsv`); that is expected, do not commit them. ### Without a Mac: the shell plus the packaging tool Download our prebuilt "shell" package (`D2RMobile-shell.ipa`), which contains no game content, from this repository's [Releases page](https://github.com/jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile/releases), add your own game files, make the install package on Windows or Linux, then sign and install it with a sideloading tool. On this route only, because the computer making the package has no Apple shader compiler, the **first launch** on the phone spends about 7 minutes compiling shaders (once, with a progress bar); a package built with Xcode has no such step. The steps, and how far each one has been verified, are in [docs/NO_XCODE.md](docs/NO_XCODE.md). ## Known limitations | Item | Status | |---|---| | Online play | Out of scope; fully offline | | Game packages in `.nsp` format | Not verified (only `.xci` was tested) | | Signing and installing with a sideloading tool (Sideloadly, AltStore and the like) | Not verified; open an issue and tell us how it went | | Making the package on Linux | Not verified (verified on Windows and Mac) | | The "one-line verdict" and "legacy Chinese name" entries in item notes | These two content tables are not shipped with the repository; you can supply your own, see `dm/ios/tools/annot/README.md` | ## Contributing and feedback - If you hit a problem, open an issue (there is a template); attaching the file exported by Share Diagnostics in the pause menu helps the most. - For the items marked not verified, tell us whether they worked or not. Either answer is valuable. - To change the code: get the test entry points above passing first. Every change has to pass the regression gates. **Taking it to other platforms:** this approach is not limited to iPhone and iPad. It ports directly to Apple silicon Macs — our daily regression tests run the very same package on a Mac. Android phones use the same class of processor, so the game program executes natively there as well, and the route is fully open: the only parts to replace are the sides of the host and the graphics layer that face the platform. The author has no Android phone at hand, and would love to see someone bring it to Android. ## Documentation by part | Document | Covers | |---|---| | [dm/README.md](dm/README.md) | How the whole thing works, directory layout, common commands, the host's source files | | [dm/gfx/README.md](dm/gfx/README.md) | The graphics layer and the shader translation chain | | [dm/ios/README.md](dm/ios/README.md) | The iOS shell, building and smoke testing | | [dm/verify/README.md](dm/verify/README.md) | What each verification tool checks and what it needs | | [docs/GAME_FILES.md](docs/GAME_FILES.md) | Game files: which ones you need, how to get them from your own console, where to put them | | [docs/DEPENDENCIES.md](docs/DEPENDENCIES.md) | Dependencies and third-party licenses | | [docs/NO_XCODE.md](docs/NO_XCODE.md) | Building without Xcode and without a Mac | | [docs/DERIVED.md](docs/DERIVED.md) | Game-related material in this repository: what is here, what is not, and why | ## Legal **You must own the game, including the Reign of the Warlock expansion.** This is an independent, non-commercial project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Blizzard Entertainment or Nintendo. Diablo and Blizzard Entertainment are trademarks of Blizzard Entertainment, Inc.; Nintendo Switch is a trademark of Nintendo. Use it only with a copy of the game that you own. ## License MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE). Third-party code keeps its own license in its own directory; see [docs/DEPENDENCIES.md](docs/DEPENDENCIES.md).

items.readme: # dsh-ops **中文** | [English](README.en.md) Windows DSH 的性能工具插件：提供独立 bash / PowerShell 7，并用 Rust 重写文件检索与批处理， 减少反复踩 PowerShell 报错所浪费的 token、时间和模型注意力。 > tips：本项目的 ops 是广义 operations（运行操作）的缩写，代指本插件处于 dsh 和系统/代码/文件操作的基础工具位置。本项目不是 operations（运维）插件。 **0.3.0 仅支持 Windows x64**，目标宿主 DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`。原生 Rust 文件/PTC worker 随包携带；PTC 默认关闭，须显式启用。Linux/macOS/ARM64 留待后续版本。见 [PTC 设计与使用](docs/native-ptc.md)。 有问题可以加qq群：1127808570 --- ## 核心特性 - （全平台）使用 Rust 编写的一组工具，用于改善 AI 报错循环、强迫思考不交付、注意力涣散的问题，并以渐进式披露减少系统 prompt 的工具定义占用：加速任务运行，减少不必要的输入输出，减少报错率，以及提供与 DSH 对齐的权限机制。 在自用 benchmark 中获得了 - 97% token 减免（开启 ops 插件的 PTC 专用工具 对比 Windows 原装标准模式） - 65% token 减免（开启 ops 插件的 PTC 专用工具 对比 Linux 原装 PTC 模式） 的成绩，并改善了在 DSH 运行的 AI 的智力表现。 - （仅 Windows）提供独立 **bash 5.3.15** 和独立 **PowerShell 7.6.6**：优先使用 bash，必要时回退 pwsh 7，让你的 AI 不再和 PowerShell 打架 —— **不修改系统默认终端、PATH 或宿主原有 shell 工具名称**，环境变量安全。 - 独立的 Rust 原生文件工具与安全批处理（**默认关闭**，须显式启用），见 [组件参考](docs/组件参考.md)。 - 未来会加入一系列 docx、pdf 处理轻量化的好用 Rust 工具，均可开关，不占用上下文。 执行顺序：**工具包 → bash → PowerShell 7**。 --- ## 快速开始 ### 前置条件 - **Node.js `^22.19 || >=24`**（`package.json` 的 `engines` 要求） - Windows x64 - 目标 DSH 应用已初始化 ### 安装 **方式一：官方插件市场（推荐）** 在目标 DSH 应用的插件市场中输入 npm 包名 **`dsh-ops`**，安装后选择启用。安装归属于当前运行的 profile，桌面端为 `desktop`。 **方式二：npm 一键安装** ```console npx --yes dsh-ops@latest install --profile desktop ``` 必须显式选择目标 profile；`tui` 映射到 **dsh-TUI 产品的 `dsh-tui` profile**，不是旧的 `tui` 目录。请先初始化目标应用。 桌面端必须使用桌面应用自带的 CLI；默认探测 `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\DeepSeek Harness\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd`。安装在其它位置时加 `--dsh-cli "<安装目录>\resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd"`。 > ⚠️ **`node_modules/@dsh-ops/` 下没有 `bash-win32-x64` 不是安装损坏。** 三个载荷都是精确钉版的**可选依赖**（`optionalDependencies`）：若你的 registry 未同步该平台包的对应版本，包管理器会**静默跳过**它——安装仍以退出码 0 结束，且不打印任何指向缺包的警告。 > **不要**用 `allowSystemShellFallback: true` 绕过：那是安全姿态降级（改用未固定摘要的系统 bash），且首次升级启动的配置迁移会把它改回 `false`。 > 普通 DSH CLI 不能管理保留的 `desktop` profile；不要把它与桌面自带入口混淆。 详情与兜底办法见 [常见问题](docs/常见问题.md)。 ### 卸载与查看状态 ```console npx --yes dsh-ops@latest status --profile desktop npx --yes dsh-ops@latest uninstall --profile desktop ``` 把 `desktop` 换成 `web` 或 `tui` 即可。 --- ## 组件 Bundle 声明四个组件，分别启停，首次安装默认开启前两个： | 组件 | 介绍 | 默认 | 发布的工具 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `dsh-ops/shell` | 将默认终端改为 bash，以及 bash 覆盖不到时提供 PowerShell 7 | 开 | `ops_bash`；宿主 `pwsh` 使用随包 PowerShell 7 | | `dsh-ops/file` | 更快、更高性能、输出更精简更省 token 的 Rust 文件检索 | 开 | 四个文件工具 | | `dsh-ops/background` | 为科研仿真、模型训练及其他长进程后台任务提供托管 | 关 | 启动、输出、列出、终止后台任务 | | `dsh-ops/ptc` | 独立 Rust 安全批处理和有界结果引用，仅纯 PTC 会话加载 | 关 | `ops_batch`、`ops_result` | “默认终端改为 bash”指模型提示优先使用 `ops_bash`，**不修改系统默认终端、PATH 或宿主原有 shell 工具名称**。 工具的完整参数、配置项与权限要求见 [组件参考](docs/组件参考.md) 与 [配置参考](docs/配置参考.md)。 > 配置迁移的完成标记：完成后重启/热加载不再覆盖；你之后主动改回 `true` 会被保留。不要删除迁移标记，否则会重新自检。 --- ## 详细文档 | 想了解 | 看这里 | | --- | --- | | 安装、更新、卸载的完整流程与全部选项 | [docs/使用指南.md](docs/使用指南.md) | | 配置项逐个说明、哪个键属于哪个组件 | [docs/配置参考.md](docs/配置参考.md) | | 四个组件分别发布什么工具、参数与权限 | [docs/组件参考.md](docs/组件参考.md) | | 报错怎么读、装不上怎么办、常见问题 | [docs/常见问题.md](docs/常见问题.md) | | 原生 PTC 的设计与使用 | [docs/native-ptc.md](docs/native-ptc.md) | | 版本变更历史 | [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) | | 来源与载荷许可记录 | [PROVENANCE.md](PROVENANCE.md) | --- ## 许可证 插件源码分发采用 **`MIT AND Apache-2.0`**：`vendor/fastctx/` 之外为 MIT；vendored FastCtx 为 Apache-2.0。见 [NOTICE](NOTICE)、`vendor/fastctx/LICENSE-APACHE` 与 `vendor/fastctx/NOTICE`。 独立的 Windows 载荷包另按上游组件许可证分发：Git for Windows 包含 GPL 等许可组件，PowerShell 包含 MIT 与第三方组件。其原始许可证、声明及来源记录随载荷保留；插件的 MIT 许可不替代这些许可。详见 [PROVENANCE.md](PROVENANCE.md)。 ## 致谢 Rust 工具基于 [yc-duan](https://github.com/yc-duan) 的 Codex 插件 FastCtx 并使用其源代码。vendor 标识与删除型分发改动记在 [vendor/fastctx/FORK.md](vendor/fastctx/FORK.md) 和 [vendor/fastctx/UPSTREAM.md](vendor/fastctx/UPSTREAM.md)。需要转载的 FastCtx 声明如下： > This product includes FastCtx > (https://github.com/yc-duan/fastctx), Copyright (c) 2026 yc-duan, > used under the Apache License 2.0. > > FastCtx is redistributed and/or modified here by the maintainer of > this distribution. Any such change is that maintainer's own work > and their sole responsibility. It is not endorsed by, not > supported by, and not attributable to the author of FastCtx, who > accepts no liability of any kind arising from this distribution or > from anything built on top of it. ## Star 趋势 [![Star 趋势图](https://api.star-history.com/svg?repos=T-Auto/dsh-ops&type=Date)](https://star-history.com/#T-Auto/dsh-ops&Date)

items.readme:
# USD BRep

Standalone Omniverse repo containing USD BRep (NURBS boundary-representation solid modeling) libraries.

## Requirements

- [**Git**](https://git-scm.com/downloads) and [**Git LFS**](https://git-lfs.com/): Git LFS is required for the large binary fixtures tracked in `.gitattributes` (USD assets, STEP/IGES/JT models).

- **(Windows - C++ Only) Microsoft Visual Studio (2019 or 2022)** with the MSVC C++ toolset:
  - Install from [Visual Studio Downloads](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/) (or **Build Tools for Visual Studio**) with the **Desktop development with C++** workload selected. A VS install without the C++ toolset is not enough.
  - The build uses this **host-installed** compiler (`msbuild.link_host_toolchain` in `repo.toml`), not Packman `msvc`.
  - `msbuild.vs_version` is pinned to `vs2019`, so VS 2022 users also need the **MSVC v142 build tools** component.
  - If discovery fails, set `msbuild.vs_path`, `msbuild.vs_version`, or both — see [repo_build toolchains](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/kit/docs/repo_build/latest/docs/toolchains.html). These settings locate an installed toolset; they do not install one.

- **(Windows - C++ Only) Windows SDK**: Install alongside MSVC via the Visual Studio Installer. If discovery fails, set `msbuild.winsdk_path` in `repo.toml`.

- **(Windows) [Microsoft Visual C++ Redistributable](https://learn.microsoft.com/cpp/windows/latest-supported-vc-redist)**: Required to run the built binaries, which link the VC runtime dynamically rather than bundling it. The **Desktop development with C++** workload above ships the redistributable, so a machine set up to build already has it — install it separately only on machines that run the binaries without Visual Studio.

- **(Linux) build-essential**: `sudo apt-get install build-essential`

All other build-time dependencies — OpenUSD, Python 3.12, pybind11, **premake**, and the `repo_*` tools — are pulled automatically via Packman when you build.

## Using this repo

Prerequisites are listed under [Requirements](#requirements). Use `./repo.sh` on Linux and macOS, `./repo.bat` on Windows. macOS: [macOS local development](#macos-local-development).

### Build it

Run prebuild before building a fresh checkout or after deleting `_build`. It stages
the omniSolid schema plugin in `_build/schema/omniSolid/resources`; `repo build`
alone does not create these resources, which USD tools require at runtime.

```bash
# Linux
./prebuild.sh
./repo.sh build

# macOS
./prebuild.sh -p macos-universal
./repo.sh build -p macos-universal

# Windows
./prebuild.bat
./repo.bat build
```

### Test it

```bash
./repo.sh test
./tests.sh linux-x86_64              # or macos-universal
```

### Format it

```bash
./repo.sh format
```

### Run the Python GUI

```bash
# Debug binaries by default (kernel Dump() echoes to the terminal).
uv run --locked --group gui python tools/scripts/smlib_gui.py

# Release binaries: add --release
uv run --locked --group gui python tools/scripts/smlib_gui.py --release
```

See `tools/smlib_gui/README.md` for smoke-test and troubleshooting commands.

### Explore examples

Runnable compositions organized by API layer live under [Examples](Examples/README.md).

## macOS local development

Apple Silicon only: `./repo.sh build -p macos-universal`. Build symlinks host Packman Python into `_build/target-deps/python` when available (`SMLIB_PYTHON_ROOT` to override).

**Python-only (default):** kernel, C++ tests, `_smlib_tests`, and `_smlib_dev` (imports need Tier 1 `_omni_solid`). No OpenUSD, OCCT, or `_omni_solid`.

```bash
./repo.sh build -p macos-universal -j10
./tests.sh macos-universal
```

**Tier 1 (optional):** local OpenUSD 3.12 staged via `setup-macos-local-deps.sh`.

```bash
export SMLIB_USD_ROOT=~/opt/usd-25.11-py312
./tools/scripts/setup-macos-local-deps.sh
./repo.sh build -p macos-universal -j10
./tests.sh macos-universal
```

Set `PYTHONPATH="$PWD/_build/macos-universal/release"` to import Python extensions. Packman OpenUSD/Python packages are not available on macOS. The macOS premake package (`premake@5.0.0-beta1+nv1-macos-universal`, `deps/host-deps.packman.xml`) is not on the public Packman server either; supply it through a user-level Packman configuration. Avoid `./repo.sh build -x`; delete `_build`, `_compiler`, and `_repo` to clean.

## Contributing

This project is currently not accepting contributions.

Issues and bug reports are welcome through the project issue tracker, and security
issues should be reported as described in `SECURITY.md`. See `CONTRIBUTING.md` for
details.

## License

USD BRep is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. See
[LICENSE](LICENSE) for the terms governing use, reproduction, and distribution.

Copyright (c) 2020-2026, NVIDIA CORPORATION & AFFILIATES. All rights reserved.

`repo.sh`, `repo.bat`, and `tools/repoman/repoman_bootstrapper.py` are licensed
under the MIT License instead; see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` for the full text.

For third-party notices and bundled components, see `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

## Heal USD BRep assets

`usd.heal_file` heals BrepArray definitions in the layers used by the current USD
composition and writes the scene with the healed geometry, keeping its layers,
references, native instancing, transforms and materials. External layers used only
by unselected variants remain referenced but are not healed. Material subset
opinions outside the BRep's defining prim spec are rejected rather than lost.

```python
import usd_brep
usd_brep.usd.heal_file("input.usdc", "input_healed.usdc")
```

适用：Claude Code / Codex / Cursor / OpenClaw（agent 技能）+ 人类手动使用 - 内容：可跟跑的作者案例、强制配方、姿势大胆度阶梯（L0–L3）、完整依赖与安装指南 --- ## 效果展示 ### 本配方输出：同一海边场景的三级对照（L0 → L1 → L2） | L0 · 全着装，无 LoRA（提示词即全部） | L1 · 湿身泳装 + LoRA@1.0 | L2 · 极低机位 + 湿身蹲姿 + LoRA@1.0 | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | 三张图同场景递进：L0 只有提示词；L1 加 LoRA + 显式皮肤/水珠描写；L2 再加低机位与开合姿态。**LoRA 负责质感，提示词负责信息密度，机位负责大胆度。** ### NSFW 效果（⚠️ 以下图片包含裸露内容） **作者原图**（Civitai showcase，本配方复刻的目标）： | 作者 · 淋浴（tawsLoRa） | 作者 · 按摩（tawsLoRa） | 作者 · 自拍（TheseAlpacas） | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | 用 §「快速开始」的命令可复刻淋浴那张（复刻输出已验证与作者原图同场景同构图，见 `downloads/samples/phase5_meta.json` 与本文快速开始一节）。 ### 3D 人偶精确姿势（Route ④，136 姿势库） 默认人物图 `references/src_standing.png`；姿势 = 骨骼旋转 JSON（MakeHuman 网格 + three.js 渲染）， 换姿势且保身份。姿势库来源：HuggingFace 4 个公开仓库（`Totemistyk/General_Poses`、 `Totemistyk/Ballet_PoseStudio`、`MIUProject/VNCCS_PoseLibrary_Main`、 `MIUProject/MySuperPoseRepo`）+ 55 个手工精选，共 **136 个**。 --- ## 快速开始（作者案例跟跑） 前置安装见 [install/setup.md](install/setup.md)。装好后一条命令复刻作者淋浴样图（~5 分钟）： ```bash python3 scripts/qwen_pose_test.py \ --mode t2i --name author_case_shower \ --prompt "$(cat prompts/taws_v13_shower.txt)" \ --seed 80964 \ --steps 50 --cfg 2.5 --sampler er_sde --scheduler beta \ --width 1152 --height 1728 \ --lora "qwen2_1-femaledVaginus-nsfw-v1_3-fine_L22-31.safetensors" \ --lora-strength 1.0 \ --out outputs/author_case/shower.png ``` 对比对象：`downloads/samples/taws_v13_shower_author.jpg`。 完整元数据（提示词/参数/seed/完整工作流）：`downloads/samples/phase5_meta.json`。 ## 三条路线 | 需求 | 路线 | 命令 | | --- | --- | --- | | 新 NSFW/性感图（文字出图） | ① T2I + NSFW LoRA（必开） | `scripts/qwen_pose_test.py --mode t2i` | | 已有角色图换姿势（保脸/保服装） | ② Edit | `scripts/qwen_pose_test.py --mode edit` | | 指定 3D 姿势库里的精确姿势 | ④ VNCCS PoseStudio | `scripts/run_vnccs_ui.py --pose ` | 姿势怎么选（大胆度阶梯 L0–L3、用户要求→姿势族映射表）：见 `SKILL.md` §4，或 `scripts/run_vnccs_ui.py --list-poses` 列出全部 136 个姿势。 ## 配方要点（摘要） -
